dissents.topic: Severity of the duplicated DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE constant across pipeline.py, CellMetadataEditor.tsx, and Commands.ts

positions.position: P0 — defeats the entire patch; the RPC was added specifically for single-source-of-truth and is then nullified by two hardcoded TS literals
P0 — ADT contract for 'the system's default base image' demands exactly one declaration; this is a fundamental invariant violation
P0 — wrong data structure: one value with one owner has been modeled as three independent values that will drift
P1 — the centralization goal is defeated but framed as a literate-programming/maintenance issue rather than a blocker
P1 — EASY-NOT-SIMPLE: looks like centralization but the fact is still complected across three locations
P1 — violates the single-source-of-truth invariant the author appears to want, falsified on introduction

dissents.topic: Severity of the _set_base_image behavior change from '' to DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE

positions.position: P0 — silent semantic change that overrides KFP's default for every user who hit the failure path; belongs in its own patch with justification or revert
P0 — postcondition weakened in observability; consumers can no longer distinguish 'unset' from 'default chosen'
P0 — UNREASONED and TESTED-NOT-PROVED change of postcondition with no stated invariant
P1 — load-bearing invariant change that needs a stated comment and a regression test
P1 — time semantics of the default shifted from render-time to config-time; needs an explicit statement of intent
P1 — collapses a meaningful tri-state and contradicts the surviving 'Use kfp default image' comment

dissents.topic: Whether the Input-to-Dialog UI swap is acceptable

positions.position: P1 regression — more clicks for the common case; placeholder on the existing Input would deliver the same goal with zero added friction
P1 — EASY-NOT-SIMPLE: dialogs feel cleaner but hide the value; an inline placeholder would have sufficed
P1 — too much framework for editing one string; Dialog/DialogTitle/DialogContent machinery adds no value over a placeholder
P1 — UNREASONED at the UX layer; no stated precondition/postcondition for why indirection is correct
P2 — workflow regression but framed as 'reconsider whether the dialog earns its complexity', not a blocker
Not flagged as a UX regression per se; flagged instead as a precondition-tightening issue (button disabled on empty stepName)

issues.description: DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE literal 'python:3.12' duplicated across pipeline.py, CellMetadataEditor.tsx, and Commands.ts fallback — single source of truth violated on introduction
issues.detail: The constant exists in backend/kale/pipeline.py (DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE), is re-declared as export const DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE in labextension/src/widgets/cell-metadata/CellMetadataEditor.tsx, and is hardcoded as the catch-arm return value in labextension/src/lib/Commands.ts getDefaultBaseImage. The entire stated rationale for the RPC is to centralize the value, but three independent copies must now be kept in lockstep; a future bump to python:3.13 will silently leave two stale literals behind. Pick one owner (backend RPC) and have the frontend either error visibly on RPC failure or treat any literal as a clearly-labeled last-resort. Torvalds, Liskov, and Pike rate P0; Knuth, Hickey, and Dijkstra rate P1.

issues.description: _set_base_image silently changes failure-path semantics from '' (defer to KFP default) to DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE='python:3.12'
issues.detail: Previously, when pod introspection failed (NotInClusterError / ApiException / missing pod), self.base_image was set to '' with a comment 'Use kfp default image', letting downstream/template resolution fall through to KFP's own default. The diff now writes DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE unconditionally, pinning python:3.12 and collapsing the distinction between 'we could not determine an image' and 'we chose python:3.12'. The surviving 'Use kfp default image' comment is now a lie. This is a behavior change masquerading as a refactor; it deserves its own patch, a stated invariant, and a regression test. Torvalds/Liskov/Dijkstra rate P0; Knuth/Hickey/Pike rate P1.

issues.description: Three independent patches submitted as one — default-constant plumbing, pipeline.py semantic change, and UI rework
issues.detail: The diff bundles (1) introducing DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE + RPC + template variable, (2) silently changing _set_base_image fallback semantics, and (3) replacing an inline Input with a Button+Dialog UI. Each has its own risk profile and review surface; the UI rework in particular is unrelated to surfacing a default. Split them so each can be evaluated and reverted independently.

issues.description: Effective-base-image resolution chain reimplemented at three sites with subtly different fallbacks
issues.detail: The precedence step.config.base_image -> pipeline base_image -> default appears in (a) nb_function_template.jinja2 as 'step.config.base_image or base_image or default_base_image', (b) InlineMetadata.createBaseImageText as 'baseImage || pipelineBaseImage || defaultBaseImage || DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE', and (c) the dialog placeholder in CellMetadataEditor as 'pipelineBaseImage || defaultBaseImage || DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE'. These must agree forever or the UI will misrepresent what actually runs. Extract a single pure resolver function returning {image, source} and call it from every site, including the template if possible.

issues.description: isDefault label is wrong whenever a pipeline-level base_image is set
issues.detail: In createBaseImageText, isDefault is computed as !this.props.baseImage, but effectiveImage may resolve to pipelineBaseImage, which is not the default but the pipeline-level override. The UI will display 'Base Image: <pipeline image> (default)' for steps inheriting the pipeline image, which is misleading. Compute source explicitly (cell / pipeline / default) and label accordingly, or only show '(default)' when neither step nor pipeline image is set.

issues.description: createBaseImageText now always renders, breaking its prior 'empty when no baseImage' contract
issues.detail:
Previously the method returned '' when this.props.baseImage was falsy, so cells without a base image rendered no paragraph. The new code unconditionally returns a

with effectiveImage and a '(default)' suffix, so every existing notebook step cell now displays a 'Base Image: python:3.12 (default)' line it never had before. The PR description promises 'display the default base image' but the visual contract has widened for every existing user. Gate the render on whether the cell is a step or whether a base-image source actually exists.

issues.description: IMAGE button replaces inline Input with a modal Dialog — workflow regression, more clicks for the common case
issues.detail: The old UI exposed Base Image as an inline 25%-wide Input; the new UI hides it behind a small button labeled 'IMAGE' that opens a modal Dialog with DialogTitle/DialogContent/DialogActions plus an internal Input and 'Reset to Default' button. Common case (set/edit a custom image) now requires 2-3 clicks instead of 1, and the value is hidden from the inline editor. If the goal was to surface the default, a placeholder on the existing Input would deliver it with zero extra clicks and far less code. Torvalds/Hickey/Pike/Dijkstra rate P1; Knuth rates P2 ('reconsider whether the dialog earns its complexity').

issues.description: IMAGE button disabled when stepName is empty — precondition silently tightened versus prior Input
issues.detail: The previous Base Image Input had no gating on stepName; the new button has disabled={!(this.props.stepName && this.props.stepName.length > 0)}. Users who could previously set a base image at any time now silently cannot until they name the step, with no tooltip or helper text explaining why. The underlying updateBaseImage already handles empty stepName via this.props.stepName || ''. Either drop the constraint or surface it to the user.

issues.description: getDefaultBaseImage swallows all RPC errors and returns hardcoded 'python:3.12'
issues.detail: The try/catch in Commands.getDefaultBaseImage conflates 'RPC unreachable', 'kernel busy', 'server returned wrong type', etc. into a silent success returning the pinned literal — defeating the RPC's purpose as source of truth. If the backend ever bumps the default and the RPC fails, the UI will lie. Either propagate the error (render 'unknown'/degraded state) or accept that the literal is a pinned cross-language contract and document it explicitly.

issues.description: Template fallback chain has redundant rungs after the pipeline.py change
issues.detail: nb_function_template.jinja2 still evaluates 'step.config.base_image or base_image or default_base_image'. After the pipeline.py change, base_image is now invariantly non-empty (always DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE on failure), so the third rung is unreachable in practice. Either remove the rung, or revert the pipeline.py change and let the template be the single resolution point. Two layers of defaulting with overlapping responsibility is a 'where does the contract live' problem.

issues.description: RPC endpoint added to return a single constant — round-trip and plumbing pay cost without buying consistency
issues.detail: get_default_base_image is a new RPC whose only behavior is to import DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE and return it, accompanied by new Commands method with try/catch, new IProps wiring through three components, and new state in LeftPanel — all to surface one string. Existing pipeline/notebook metadata endpoints could carry this value, or the template (which already has it) could render it server-side. The added RPC pays cost without buying consistency, because the frontend hardcodes the same literal as a fallback anyway. Knuth/Torvalds rate it P2/P1, Pike P2.

issues.description: Button width:'5%' with text 'IMAGE' inside hand-tuned wrapper div — style violates surrounding code's conventions and will render inconsistently
issues.detail: The new control is a contained primary Button sized 'small' with style={{ width: '5%' }} wrapped in a <div style={{ padding: 0, marginRight: '4px' }}>. 5% of the parent will almost certainly clip or overflow the word 'IMAGE'; the label 'IMAGE' is also shouty/ambiguous (image of what?) and inconsistent with the surrounding Input/Select controls that use sensible percentages. Match the layout conventions or own a coherent redesign. Torvalds rates P1; Knuth/Liskov/Pike/Dijkstra rate P2.

issues.description: Reset-to-Default writes empty string and relies on fragile truthy-check semantics downstream
issues.detail: 'Reset to Default' calls updateBaseImage('') which depends on every downstream consumer (createBaseImageText, template) treating '' as 'use default'. If anyone ever stores '' deliberately, or validation rejects empty, this breaks silently. Prefer null/undefined or an explicit sentinel resolved through one helper. Dijkstra notes the user has no way to predict from the dialog which fallback value will be displayed after reset.

issues.description: Local 'from kale.pipeline import DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE' inside get_default_base_image RPC
issues.detail: The import is placed inside the function body with no comment explaining why (circular import? lazy load?). compiler.py already imports DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE at module top, so there is no apparent cycle. Hoist the import to module scope or add a one-line comment naming the cycle being broken. This obscures the module's declared dependencies.

issues.description: Reordering createBaseImageText and createLimitsText in InlineMetadata.render with no rationale
issues.detail: The render output now emits createLimitsText() before createBaseImageText() where previously base image came first. Unrelated to the feature, and unjustified in the commit message. Drive-by reorderings make blame archaeology harder and bisects noisier.

issues.description: stepDependencies select width shuffled from 35% to 30% with no holistic layout pass
issues.detail: The Select width was nudged from 35% to 30% and a 5%-wide IMAGE button added, with the rest of the row layout untouched. The arithmetic of the row layout is now implicit — what fills the remaining space? Magic-number tuning by eye rather than a flex/grid container; either own the row layout or leave it alone.

issues.description: DefaultState.defaultBaseImage initialized to '' forces every consumer to re-coalesce against the literal
issues.detail: Initializing defaultBaseImage to empty string in LeftPanel state means every read site must guard with || DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE. Initialize to the known fallback so the data carries a usable value at all times and consumers can simply use it. Symptomatic of modeling one value as multiple sentinels.

issues.description: No tests added for the new behavior — constant, RPC, template variable, resolution chain, or pipeline.py semantic change
issues.detail: A new constant, a new template variable, a new RPC endpoint, and a quiet postcondition change in _set_base_image all ship without tests. Minimally: a unit test that the compiler renders default_base_image into the template when both step.config.base_image and pipeline base_image are unset; a test pinning the new _set_base_image fallback behavior; a test of the frontend resolution order. As Dijkstra puts it, equivalence with the prior behavior is not asserted — TESTED-NOT-PROVED at best, not even tested at worst.

synthesis.summary: All six reviewers converge on two findings, though they split on severity: (1) the headline 'single source of truth for DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE' is violated on arrival — the literal 'python:3.12' is declared in pipeline.py, re-declared in CellMetadataEditor.tsx, and hardcoded as the swallowed-error fallback in Commands.ts — and (2) _set_base_image silently changes the failure-path postcondition from '' (defer to KFP default) to a concrete pinned 'python:3.12', a semantic shift buried in what was advertised as a UI feature, with no test and a now-lying inline comment. Torvalds, Liskov, and Dijkstra rate one or both of these P0 and recommend REFUSE/NEEDS-WORK; Knuth/Hickey/Pike rate them P1 but reach the same architectural verdict. Beyond those, the panel agrees the resolution chain (cell -> pipeline -> default) is reimplemented at three sites with subtle differences, the '(default)' label is provably wrong when a pipeline-level image is set, the Input-to-Dialog UI swap is a workflow regression that a placeholder on the existing Input would have avoided, and the new IMAGE button has both an unjustified disabled-on-empty-stepName precondition and a 5% width that won't render coherently. The largest preserved disagreement is severity-level, not direction: Torvalds frames this as three patches glued together that should be split and largely deleted, while Knuth/Hickey/Pike frame it as a centralization-that-failed-to-centralize that needs one resolver function and one source of truth — they want fewer moving parts, not necessarily a revert.
